messages.subject: Errors in multidata processing
parts:

parts:
Dear all,

The problem was partially solved!
It turned out that previously I was wrong with the milestone data. I used 4 data in one folder to test whether it went well or not. And then I put all 130 data in that folder. Finally, it failed.
This time, I initially processed one data as milestone data and then put all 130 data in the folder. It was successfully done. The output CSV files were correct and the visual reports were generated. However, It still has warning messages. Is that a problem?
   
Generate visual reports

GGIR is now creating a visualreport (pdf) for each of the 129 recordings as a final step in the GGIR pipeline. This can take a while as it is done file-by-file. If you do not want the visualreports then you can kill the process (Ctrl-C or ESC) as that will not affect the rest of the analyses and reports. To avoid this next time,  change Boolean argument 'visualreport' to FALSE.Warning messages:
1:
Ignoring argument/parameter rawaccfiles_formats as stored in the configuration file as no (longer) used by GGIR. To avoid this warning remove the corresponding rows from the config.csv file.

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: Errors in multidata processing
parts: It seems that if there is another new raw CSV file, all analyses should be redone. Is that right? Or is there another solution?

If you set parameter overwrite = FALSE, GGIR will only process the files that it has not processed yet. So, no need to reprocess the other files unless you changed other parameters related to the GGIR part you are running. For example, if you first run part 1 with do.enmo = TRUE, and later decide to set this to FALSE and set do.mad = TRUE then you will have to reprocess all the data for part 2 to be able to append the results.

Best,

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/
